summary: Boat radio gear: VHF, SSB and SITOR, survival beacons, weather fax, NAVTEX and NMEA networks.

blocks.title: VHF: nearby contacts
items: Channels near 156 MHz sit 25 kHz apart.
FM deviation: the voice's swing, at most ±5 kHz.
Channel 16, 156.800 MHz: distress and calling by voice.
Channel 70, 156.525 MHz: DSC and acknowledgement only, no voice.
USA-INT: USA changes some duplex channels into simplex. INT restores duplex. Neither adds range.
GPS check: latitude and longitude, plus speed, on the VHF display.

items.name: Carson's rule: FM bandwidth
items.means: Deviation plus top voice pitch, doubled.

blocks.title: MF and HF: long range
items: SSB: single sideband. No carrier, one sideband: all the power goes into your voice.
Voice test: current surges with each syllable. The ammeter swings up, voltage drops, and panel indicator lamps may glow.
Tuner: matches the antenna to each frequency, then holds.

blocks.title: Weather fax and NAVTEX
items: Facsimile: printed pictures for permanent display on paper.
HF weather fax, 3 to 23 MHz: 120 lines per minute, frequency-shift keying with an 800 Hz shift.
Filter: crystal lattice band-pass, 1 kHz at -6 dB.
NAVTEX: 518 kHz. Receives MSI in SITOR-B or FEC mode. Ships never transmit.
Not printed: subject indicator matches one programmed for rejection. Navigational, weather and search and rescue messages can't be rejected.

blocks.title: NMEA data
items: NMEA 0183: serial link, one talker, multiple listeners. Grounding both shield ends makes a ground loop.
NMEA 2000: bi-directional, multi-transmitter, multi-receiver network. Backbone also carries 12 V.
Single location: end-powered network. Long backbone: feed power mid-way.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Testing with the red distress button sends a real alert.
GTO-15, not RG-8U or RG-213, feeds the backstay.
ARQ repeats only when asked. Time diversity is FEC's.
FEC broadcasts need no two-way contact with the coast station.
A SART isn't on 406 MHz or 3 GHz, and transmits only when radar interrogates it.
An EPIRB has no voice and can't say what's wrong.
